questions.stem: Martha has been trying to ______ her roommate since their quarrel last week, as she doesn’t want to continue the argument.
As David finished the last drop of the delicious chicken soup, he licked his lips and gave out sounds of ______.
After several rounds of intense fighting, the boxer punched his ______ right in the face, knocked him out, and won the match.
Watch out! The bench has just been painted. You can fan the wet paint if you want to ______ its drying.
Warm milk ______ sleepiness. So if you have trouble falling asleep, try drinking some warm milk before going to bed.
Having worked five years as a data processor in a small town, Alice is tired of the routine of her job and the ______ of her life.
Peter has never been on time to meetings or appointments. It would be interesting to look into reasons why he is ______ late.
The film Life of Pi won Ang Lee an Oscar in 2013 for Best Director—one of the most ______ awards in the movie industry.
According to environmental scientists, the earth is likely to experience significant ______ changes within the next century.
Traditional Chinese medical practices include ______ remedies, which use plants, plant parts, or a mixture of these to prevent or cure diseases.

France, home to such major fashion houses as Chanel, Dior, and Yves Saint Laurent, has joined Italy, Spain, and Israel in adopting laws against super-skinny models on catwalks or in ads.
The French government has passed a bill that will [[11]] the use of excessively skinny models. Modeling agencies violating the law can receive a fine of up to US$81,000, with up to six months in jail for staff involved. According to French officials, the measure aims to [[12]] the glorification of dangerously thin models.
Under the approved legislation, models will have to present a medical [[13]] that proves they are healthy before being allowed to work in the fashion industry. Moreover, they will be [[14]] regular weight checks. Modeling agencies will have to produce a medical report showing that their models have maintained a [[15]] body mass-to-height ratio. This bill is expected to change young women’s view on the ideal female form.

groups.passage:
One factor that separates a living thing from an inanimate object is the organism’s ability to carry out chemical reactions that are crucial for its survival. Imagine the infinite amount of reactions that a large organism such as human carries out every single day. [[16]] of these reactions are possible without enzymes.
Enzymes consist of various types of proteins that work to drive the chemical reactions [[17]] for certain types of nutrients to take effect. Enzymes can either launch a reaction or speed it up. In the absence of enzymes, reactants may take hundreds of years to convert into a usable product, if they are able to do so [[18]]. This is why enzymes are crucial in the sustenance of life on earth.
Enzymes, [[19]], do not always function perfectly. In 1902 Sir Archibald Garrod was the first to attribute a [[20]] to an enzyme defect, which he later referred to as an “inborn error of metabolism.” Today, newborns are routinely screened for certain enzyme defects such as PKU (phenylketonuria) and galactosemia, an error in the handling of the sugar galactose.

tags.topic: enzymes and the chemical reactions of living things

groups.passage:
Hundreds of years ago, a savory idea—called the century egg—was hatched in rural China. As the story goes, a farmer found naturally preserved duck eggs in a muddy pool of water and slaked lime. After surviving a tasting, he set out to replicate them manually, resulting in a [[21]] that would endure for centuries as a comfort food in Hong Kong, China and parts of Southeast Asia.
Though details of the century egg’s discovery are undocumented, scientists estimate that it [[22]] more than 500 years to the Ming Dynasty. And aside from some techniques used for large-scale production today, the egg preservation process has remained relatively [[23]].
To make the eggs, a vat is typically filled with a combination of strong black tea, lime, salt and freshly burned wood ashes, and left to cool overnight. The next day, duck, quail, or chicken eggs are added to the [[24]]. Then they soak anywhere from seven weeks to five months—not for a century as the name [[25]].
The century egg also [[26]] many other names, such as hundred-year egg, thousand-year egg, or millennium egg. But no matter what it’s called, this common snack has a rather uncommon taste and is often grouped by travelers with other [[27]] Asian foods such as chicken feet or snake soup. Getting beyond the egg’s appearance is the first [[28]]. Instead of being white with a bright orange yolk, the jelly-like egg takes on a less [[29]] dark brown and swampy green hue. There’s also a pungent ammonia-like odor to contend with, which has earned the snack yet another nickname: the “horse urine egg.”
While the century egg draws a following from older generations and curious travelers, it is falling out of [[30]] with the younger set, who are weary of China’s preserved and fermented foods. The future of the humble snack is uncertain, but chefs in Chinese restaurants are still trying to preserve this nostalgic bite of culinary heritage.

tags.topic: the century egg, a traditional Chinese preserved egg

groups.passage:
One of the most difficult things for a human to face is the loss of a limb. If a person loses an arm or a leg, he/she must be fitted with an artificial limb.
The situation is very different for a starfish. If a starfish loses an arm, it can grow a new one. [[31]] Snails can even regrow their heads—imagine what the world would be like if humans could do that. But we can’t. Nor can we grow new limbs or even fingers. That’s why scientists are studying animals that can regrow body parts, that is, regenerate. [[32]]
Many different kinds of animals show some form of regeneration. Most of them are, however, limited to the sort a lizard is capable of, like regrowing a lost tail. A cockroach can grow back a missing limb, but the limb itself can’t generate a new cockroach. [[33]] Bidirectional regeneration, on the other hand, refers to a situation in which splitting of an animal will result in separate fully functional animals. [[34]] Cut a hydra in half, and you’ll get two hydras. Cut it into four pieces, and you’ll get four.
[[35]] A single one can be cut into hundreds of pieces and each will grow back into a whole in a week or so. Because of this remarkable ability, one planarian can be created over and over, giving it a sort of immortality. Whether this phenomenon can be achieved in humans will likely require years of research.

options_bank.B: Humans aren’t completely without regenerative talents.
options_bank.C: The same thing happens for lobsters, salamanders, and many other animals.
options_bank.D: When it comes to regeneration, few animals can equal the magic of the planarian.
options_bank.E: This type of regeneration is demonstrated in a few animals, such as hydras and sea stars.
options_bank.F: They hope that this line of research will make regeneration possible in humans someday.

groups.passage: Often named as the most prominent contemporary female architect, Zaha Hadid, an Iraqi-born British woman, is significant for her intellectual toughness and her refusal to compromise on her artistic ideas. For many years, her designs filled the pages of architecture journals but were dismissed as impractical or too radical. Also, being female in a male-dominated field didn’t help her succeed. Despite these setbacks, her star began to rise when her design for Cincinnati’s new Center for Contemporary Art was selected and built, earning her worldwide acclaim. The New York Times described the building as “the most important new building in America since the Cold War.” Once her talent was recognized, commissions started coming in to design a variety of projects, including public transportation, libraries, and opera houses. In 2004, Hadid became the first woman to win the prestigious Pritzker Prize. She also won the Stirling Prize in 2010 and 2011. Hadid’s interest in architecture had roots in a trip her family took to the ancient Sumer region in southern Iraq, the site of one of the world’s oldest civilizations, when she was a teenager. She recalled: “The beauty of the landscape—where sand, water, reeds, birds, buildings, and people all somehow flowed together—has never left me. I’m trying to discover—invent, I suppose—an architecture, and forms of urban planning, that do something of the same thing in a contemporary way.” Nature’s forms appear as a recurrent source of inspiration for Hadid’s architecture. Her designs are daring and visionary experiments with space and with the relationships of buildings to their urban surroundings. She consistently pushes the boundaries of architecture and urban design in the pursuit of a visionary aesthetic that expresses her ideals.

groups.passage: Todd Bol, a retired businessman, could never have expected that a wooden container he built on his deck one day in 2009 would have the global impact it does today. Bol built a dollhouse-size structure that looked like a schoolhouse on a post, and he put it on his lawn as a free community library to commemorate his mother, who was a book lover and school teacher. Bol’s prototype gave birth to Little Free Library (LFL), a nonprofit organization that seeks to place small, accessible book exchange boxes in neighborhoods around the world. The concept is simple: Neighbors are invited to share a book, leave a book, or both. Today, there are over 50,000 of these libraries registered in 70 countries. Almost everyone can register with LFL and start a library as long as the person keeps it in good shape and makes sure that book materials are appropriate for his/her neighborhood. Library owners can create their own library boxes; therefore, the libraries are usually unique in appearance, and there seems to be no limit to the possibilities. One library in California was built out of a used wine crate; another in Texas had tiny stairs and bright colored walls. Once registered, libraries are assigned a number at LFL’s website. The LFL Index lists the locations of all libraries with GPS coordinates and other information. Owners receive a sign that reads “Little Free Library.” People say they have been more inclined to pick up a book when walking by a Little Free Library, out of curiosity and because it’s convenient. Some sidewalk librarians say they have met more neighbors since having a little library in their front yard. Bol is also most proud of the way Little Free Library is bringing communities together. “It’s started a neighborhood exchange. It gets people talking and more comfortable with their neighbors,” he says. “This leads to them helping each other.”

groups.passage:
The term “forensic linguistics,” in its broadest sense, covers all areas of study where language and law intersect. A famous example of its application is the case of Chris Coleman, who was suspected of killing his family in 2009. Robert Leonard, the head of the forensic linguistics program at Hofstra University, presented some important linguistic evidence in the trial against Coleman. Relying heavily on word choice and spelling, Leonard suggested that the same person had written the threatening e-mails and sprayed the graffiti, and that those samples bore similarities to Coleman’s writing style. Coleman was later found guilty of the murder.
Robert Leonard was not the first one who resorted to linguistic evidence in criminal investigation. The field of forensic linguistics was brought to prominence by his colleague James Fitzgerald in 1996 with his work in the case of the Unabomber, who had sent a series of letter bombs to college professors over several years, causing serious casualties. Working for the FBI, Fitzgerald urged the publication of the Unabomber’s letter—a lengthy declaration of the criminal’s philosophy.
After the letter was published, many people called the FBI to say they recognized the writing style. By analyzing sentence structure, word choice, and other linguistic patterns, Fitzgerald narrowed down the range of possible authors and finally linked the letter to the writings of Ted Kaczynski, a solitary former mathematician. For instance, Kaczynski tended to use extensive parallel phrases, which were frequently found in the bomber’s letter. Both Kaczynski and the bomber also showed a preference for dozens of unusual words, such as “chimerical” and “anomic.” The bomber’s use of the terms “broad” for women and “negro” for African Americans also enabled Fitzgerald to roughly calculate the suspect’s age. The linguistic evidence was strong enough for the judge to search Kaczynski’s isolated cabin in Montana; what was found there put him in prison for life.
On some level, finding hidden meanings from linguistic evidence is what we all do intuitively in our daily language interaction. This is exactly the same work forensic professionals do. As one forensic-linguistics firm, Testipro, puts it in its online promotional ad, the field can be regarded as “the basis of the entire legal system.”

groups.passage:
During the past three hundred years, when a country gains its freedom or independence, one of the first things established is a national anthem. National anthems are generally played and sung at formal state occasions and other events which celebrate or support the country’s national identity.
Holland’s 16th-century hymn “Het Wilhelmus” is widely considered the world’s oldest national anthem, followed by the U.K.’s “God Save the King/Queen”—also a hymn, popularized in the 1740s. As nationalism spread throughout Europe in the 18th and 19th centuries, so did anthems. Many countries, such as the independent states that are today part of Germany, took “God Save the King/Queen” as a model and adopted hymns (songs of prayer typically addressed to a deity or VIP). Others, notably Spain and France, chose marches (songs with a strong, regular rhythm often performed by military bands)—which expressed a martial rather than monarchic spirit. With imperialism, Europeans spread their musical taste. Even when former colonies gained independence, they often imitated the traditions of their former rulers. The result is that most anthems are either hymns or marches, played on European instruments.
Japan’s anthem makes for a good case study of European influence. In the 1860s a British bandmaster living in Japan, John William Fenton, noted that the country did not have a national anthem. A local military officer, Ōyama Iwao, selected the lyrics from a Heian era poem and Fenton wrote the melody. About a decade later, a Japanese committee chose a replacement melody by a court musician—one that had been composed for traditional Japanese instruments, but in a mixed style influenced by Fenton’s arrangement. The version in use today was also altered by German Franz Eckert to fit a Western scale.
In addition to hymns and marches, British composer Michael Bristow identifies a couple of more minor categories. National anthems in South and Central America are often operatic, with long, elaborate orchestral introductions. These were influenced by 19th-century Italian opera. Burma and Sri Lanka are both in a folk group, as they rely more on indigenous instruments.

關於評分標準，在中譯英部分，每小題總分 4 分，原則上是每個錯誤扣 0.5 分，相同的錯誤只扣一次。
今年的中譯英考題與「世界大學運動會（The Universiade）」有關，評量的重點在於考生能否運用所學的詞彙與基本句型將中文翻譯成正確、通順且達意的英文句子。由於測驗之詞彙皆為高中常用詞彙，中等程度以上的考生如果能使用正確句型，並注意用字、拼字，應能得到理想的分數。例如，「國際體育與文化盛事」若譯成 an international athletic and cultural event 就能得分；或譯成 an international event of sports and culture 也能得分；「學生運動員建立友誼」若譯成 student athletes establish friendship 就能得分。在拼字方面，少部分學生在抄寫 The Universiade 忘了 U 應該大寫，或把 athlete 寫成 athelete；把 sportsmanship 寫成 sportmanship。也有少數考生把「真諦」的…true meaning…寫成 true meanning，殊為可惜。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem: 每個人從小到大都有覺得寂寞的時刻，也都各自有排解寂寞的經驗和方法。當你感到寂寞時，有什麼人、事或物可以陪伴你，為你排遣寂寞呢？請以此為主題，寫一篇英文作文，文長至少120個單詞。文分兩段，第一段說明你會因為什麼原因或在何種情境下感到寂寞，第二段描述某個人、事或物如何伴你度過寂寞時光。
questions.scoring_notes:
「英文作文」的評分標準是依據內容、組織、文法句構、字彙拼字四個項目給分，字數明顯不足則扣總分 1 分。
今年作文題目請考生就「寂寞」這個主題及如何排解的經驗和方法表達其看法，提示為「每個人從小到大都有覺得寂寞的時刻，也都各自有排解寂寞的經驗和方法。當你感到寂寞時，有什麼人、事或物可以陪伴你，為你排遣寂寞呢？」再請考生以此為主題，寫一篇英文作文，文長至少 120 個單詞。文分兩段，第一段說明你會因為什麼原因或在何種情境下感到寂寞，第二段描述某個人、事或物如何伴你度過寂寞時光。
多數考生都能在第一段提到自己在何種情況下會感到寂寞，也大都能簡單敘述有何人陪伴自己，或自己用什麼方法度過寂寞時光，但也有部分考生對「寂寞」的定義較不精確，把「寂寞」和「無聊」視為同一件事，但整體而言，大部分的考生都能表達一些看法。而英文作文評分重點仍在於內容是否切題、是否就自己提出之觀點，提供充分、具體之事例支持、兩段文字之間是否連貫合理、句構語法及用字是否適切、以及拼字與標點符號是否使用得當。考生對於今年的作文題目大致都能有所發揮，語言能力表現佳、充分具體事例之支持應是考生得分之重要元素。

extraction.method: python-docx 讀 Word 版題本 paper-2.docx 為主（軟換行接回、空格底線改 [[題號]]），pdftotext -layout 擷取 paper-1.pdf 逐字比對，並用 Read 逐頁看 PDF 頁面影像（第 1–8 頁）核對段落、粗斜體與版面（本卷無圖表）；答案 pdftotext answer.pdf 並看頁面影像核對；評分原則 pdftotext scoring.pdf 並看頁面影像核對；統計以 xlrd 讀 stats-1.xls（英：P/Ph/Pl/D）、stats-2.xls（英：T/H/L 選項分析，* 號選項與官方答案逐題比對一致）、stats-3.xls（工作表 2：英文科非選擇題分數分布）；建檔腳本放 scratchpad，未進 repo
issues: 結構與 gsat-spec.json legacy_ast「98–110」期別一致：詞彙 1–10（各1分，10分）、綜合測驗 11–20（2篇×5題，10分）、文意選填 21–30（12個選項 A–L，10分）、篇章結構 31–35（6個選項 A–F，各2分，10分）、閱讀測驗 36–51（4篇×4題，各2分，32分）、中譯英 2題各4分（8分）、英文作文 20分（至少120個單詞）；選擇題 72分＋非選擇題 28分＝100分；考試時間 80分鐘；不倒扣。本年度第一大題題本標題為「一、詞彙（占10分）」（非「詞彙題」），與 spec 註記（僅 100 及 107–110 標為「詞彙題」）相符。
非選擇題題號：題本中譯英子題編為 1、2，英文作文不編號；因 schema 要求 no 為整數，中譯英填 no=1、2（label「中譯英1」「中譯英2」），作文填 no=1（label「英文作文」），因此 validator 出現「題號重複 [1, 2]」warning，label 皆不重複，屬預期（與 ast-107／ast-110 處理方式相同）。

中譯英：評分原則（scoring.pdf）沒有公布完整參考譯文，只舉例部分詞組的可得分譯法（「國際體育與文化盛事」an international athletic and cultural event／an international event of sports and culture；「學生運動員建立友誼」student athletes establish friendship）與常見拼字錯誤，因此兩題 answer 與 accepted_answers 均為 null（部分詞組不是完整答案，未放入 accepted_answers）。scoring_notes 逐字收錄中譯英評分通則句（每小題 4 分、每個錯誤扣 0.5 分、相同錯誤只扣一次）與整段中譯英說明；該段的例句同時涉及兩題（The Universiade、國際體育與文化盛事屬第1題；學生運動員、athlete、sportsmanship、真諦屬第2題），句子無法拆開，所以兩題放入相同內容。
英文作文：answer 依規定為 null；scoring_notes 逐字收錄評分通則句（內容、組織、文法句構、字彙拼字四項，字數明顯不足扣總分 1 分）與評分原則第2頁兩段作文說明。essay_type 標 topic（依題目文字主題寫作，與 ast-107–110 一致；ast-97–100 同型題曾標 two_paragraph），paragraphs=2。

評分原則 PDF 文字層第1頁最後一段有一行因左右對齊而在中文字與標點間插入空白（pdftotext 得「athelete； 把 sportsmanship 寫 成 sportmanship 。 也 有 少數 考 生 把 「 真 諦 」」），已依頁面影像去除中文字／全形標點之間的多餘空白，中英文之間的空白保留；跨行接合處在中文與英數字之間補一個半形空格（「扣 0.5 分」「寫成 athelete」），與同文件其他處（如「總分 4 分」）的排版一致。本檔評分原則沒有 CJK 相容表意字。

非選擇題統計：stats-3.xls 工作表「2」只有「第一題(滿分:8分)」（中譯英兩小題合計）與「第二題(滿分:20分)」（作文）的分數人數分布，無逐子題資料，也沒有答對率／鑑別度，因此放在 s6、s7 的 section 層級 stats（schema 未定義的延伸欄位，格式同 ast-107／ast-110），題目層級 stats 為 null。只收有數字的分數區間；score_range 去掉原表空白（「8.00- 8.99」→「8.00-8.99」）；本年度原表最低區間為「0.00- 0.99」（未像部分年度拆成 0.01–0.99 與 0），照原表保留。percent／cumulative_percent 為人數除以報名總人數 47,224（含缺考 1,934 人）的 0–1 小數（取 4 位），已核對與原表兩位小數百分比一致。

選擇題統計：correct_rate／high_group／low_group／discrimination 取自 stats-1.xls「英」工作表的 P、Ph、Pl、D 欄（報考 47,224、到考 45,290）；option_rates 取自 stats-2.xls「英」的 T（全體）列，另加延伸欄位 omit_rate（未答比例）與 option_rates_high／option_rates_low（H／L 列）。已逐題核對 51 題 stats-2 標 * 的選項＝answer.pdf 官方答案，且 T 列答對選項百分比＝P。原表為整數百分比，option_rates 加未答後的加總因四捨五入介於 0.99–1.02（僅第25題為 1.02）。
統計表間的微小差異：第47題低分組通過率 stats-1.xls（Pl）為 31%，stats-2.xls 低分組選答正確選項 D 為 32%（兩表各自四捨五入所致）；low_group 採 stats-1.xls，option_rates_low 照 stats-2.xls 原值。

文字以 Word 版（paper-2.docx）為主，並與 pdftotext 擷取的 PDF 文字（去空白後逐字元比對完全一致）及 PDF 頁面影像逐段核對。Word 檔中的不換行空白（U+00A0，第36–39題選文第2段 acclaim. The、第48–51題選文第1段 anthem. National）改為一般空白；Word 段落內的軟換行（第18、22、24、31、34題空格前）以空格接起。段落切分依 PDF 首行縮排判斷：第31–35題選文中 [[31]]、[[34]] 位於行首但無縮排，屬前一段的延續；[[35]] 有縮排，另起一段。空格（底線＋題號）改寫為 [[題號]]。

格式：第8題題幹的 Life of Pi 與第44–47題選文的 Testipro 為斜體；第36–39題選文第2段與第37題題幹的 her star began to rise、第40–43題選文第2段與第41題題幹的 prototype、第40／46／48題題幹的 NOT 為粗體，斜體與題幹中的粗體依規定不保留格式；第37、41題問的是粗體字（非底線），選文對應位置已加 <b> 並填 refers_to。

原文照錄：第16–20題選文「a large organism such as human carries out」（human 前無冠詞）、第50題選項 (B)「The lyrics was written by a Japanese officer.」（主詞動詞不一致）皆照題本保留；第48–51題選文 Ōyama Iwao 的 Ō（U+014C）照原字保留。文意選填選項 (I) 在 Word 為「(I)goes by」、PDF 為「( I ) goes by」，選項文字取「goes by」。英文作文 stem 取自 Word 版「提示：」之後的內容（去掉「提示：」前綴，同 ast-107–110）；PDF 文字層與頁面影像在提示「至少 120 個單詞」數字前後有間距，Word 版為「至少120個單詞」，採 Word 版：查證時核對 docx 原始 XML，提示段落使用 Word 預設的中英文自動間距（autoSpaceDE/DN），間距是排版效果，不是空白字元；說明框（樣式「說明」關閉 autoSpace）的「至少120個單詞」在 PDF 上就沒有間距，可以佐證。中譯英說明第2行的全形縮排空白、作文說明第2行的半形縮排空白已去除。
頂層 parts 為延伸欄位，保存「第壹部分：選擇題（占72分）」「第貳部分：非選擇題（占28分）」標題與第貳部分的說明文字（逐字）；封面「作答注意事項」（考試時間：80分鐘等）與各題組前的「第11至15題為題組」等字樣未另存。本卷沒有任何圖表、照片或表格（逐頁看過影像確認），figures 皆為空陣列。

標註（tags）為解析者判讀：篇章結構 clue——31 pronoun_reference（The same thing 回指海星斷肢再生，下句 Snails can even 承接）、32 pronoun_reference（They＝scientists、this line of research）、33 contrast（unidirectional 對 Bidirectional ..., on the other hand）、34 lexical_cohesion（hydras ↔ Cut a hydra in half）、35 topic_sentence（段首句引出 planarian，下句 A single one 承接）；第17題 grammar_point 為 participle（reactions required for ... 過去分詞修飾名詞）；第16題標 discourse（None 由下文 enzymes 不可或缺推得）。題組 sdgs 依主題判斷：11–15 健康體態法規 [3]、16–20 酵素與新生兒篩檢 [3]、36–39 女性建築師 [5]、40–43 社區小圖書館 [4, 11]、44–47 司法鑑識語言學 [16]、作文寂寞與排解 [3]。

查證（verifier）：獨立重新核對——51 題答案逐題對照 answer.pdf 文字層與頁面影像，全部一致；1–51 題題幹與每個選項、文意選填／篇章結構選項庫，逐字對照 Word 版（逐題結構化比對）和 PDF 文字層（連續字串比對），全部一致；8 篇選文全部逐字比對（Word 與 PDF 文字層），首末句、段落數（3/3/5/4/4/4/4/4）與 wc -w 字數（153/181/323/246/280/317/365/340）都和 pdftotext 相同，[[題號]] 位置與 PDF 頁面影像一致；7 頁頁面影像確認無圖表、段落縮排與粗斜體位置；51 題 P/Ph/Pl/D 和 T/H/L 選項比例、未答比例全部以程式對照 xls（含第47題 Pl 31% 與 L 列 32% 的差異），stats-3 兩題分數分布逐列核對；中譯英、作文題目與評分原則逐字對照 scoring.pdf 頁面影像。只修正本 issues 中「選項比例加總範圍」的敘述（原寫 0.98–1.02，實際 0.99–1.02），資料欄位本身沒有錯誤。
